source_overlay.note: Compared against the current dirty platform_task.c/h and owner-owned native_task_tests.c, not a checkout reconstructed from HEAD.

status_mapping.parity: exact for fallible bounded reservations, allocation-gate denial, and worker-start failure

type_mapping.adaptation: Opaque raw pointer becomes an owned, Clone-able safe handle around Arc-shared state.
A borrow of a stable AtomicBool prevents retention beyond callback lifetime.
One-shot safe callback receives &mut C and a borrowed token; C must be Send + 'static.
Context is retained by TaskCallback until terminal slot transition, then dropped outside the mutex.
No caller allocator pointer/context is retained.
Only bounded capacity and worker count remain; allocation hooks are replaced by safe allocation gating.
task_id becomes id and C output-pointer filling becomes an owned Option result.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Validates 1..64 capacity and 1..4 workers before allocation. Starts workers only after bounded Vec/VecDeque reservations and safe AllocationGate permits. Partial thread startup signals stop and joins every started worker before returning NoMemory.
symbols.adaptation: Custom C allocate/free callbacks map to accepted vexel_base::AllocationGate plus Vec::try_reserve_exact and std thread spawn errors. A five-point safe gate covers bounded slot, pending, handle, shared-control, and worker-owner allocations; it does not claim deterministic injection of system allocator OOM inside Arc::new or Rust runtime internals.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: A caller-created TaskCallback contains a Send+'static owned context and one-shot callback. Rejected submission returns the same TaskCallback; accepted context is dropped once outside the mutex after terminal state publication/discard.
symbols.adaptation: C borrowed void* context is replaced with an owned typed context. Shared context uses Arc<T> as the typed context. The callback receives &mut T and a lifetime-bound cancellation token, so safe code cannot retain the native token past callback execution.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Task context is owned by TaskCallback; context Drop is the cleanup operation. Rejected submission returns ownership and does not invoke the callback. The worker frees/updates the slot under lock, releases the lock, then drops the task context exactly once.
symbols.adaptation: C's optional raw cleanup function becomes Rust Drop on the typed context, with no separate raw cleanup callback.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Queued work is retired without running; running work receives an atomic cooperative cancellation signal; completed work becomes discarded. Unknown and zero IDs retain native status behavior.
symbols.adaptation: CancellationToken borrows a stable per-slot AtomicBool only for callback lifetime; no raw pointer or cloneable stale token is exposed.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Only strictly greater generations are accepted. Older queued work is discarded, running work is cooperatively canceled, and old completions cannot be polled.
symbols.adaptation: u64 generation arithmetic has no increment or wrap; the caller supplies the next generation as in C.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Returns one current-generation result and frees its slot/ID under the mutex. Failure results are retained just like success results.
symbols.adaptation: The C output pointer becomes an owned Option value; no caller-provided pointer can be invalid.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Marks stopping, signals queued/running cancellation, discards completions, drops queued owned contexts outside the mutex, and joins worker handles. Repeated concurrent shutdown is serialized by the worker-handle mutex.
symbols.adaptation: A worker callback can request shutdown without attempting to join itself; thread-local worker identity avoids deadlock with another thread that is joining it. A reentrant worker call requests stop and returns; an external shutdown joins every worker before returning.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Safe references and Arc ownership prevent destruction while a safe API borrow is active. Final owner drop requests shutdown and joins workers; callers need no separate unsafe destroy call.
symbols.adaptation: The C active-call counter/assertion and explicit destroy become Rust borrowing/Arc lifetime enforcement plus final-owner shutdown.

symbols.rust: No production counterpart; concurrent safe API lifetime exercised by shutdown_races_safely_with_cloned_api_calls_and_final_drop_joins
symbols.ownership_and_limits: The test-only C global pause gate existed to probe destroy during an admitted raw-pointer call. Rust's safe borrow/Arc ownership removes that invalid lifetime path.
symbols.adaptation: Omitted as an unsafe misuse probe; safe concurrent API calls racing shutdown are directly tested instead.

symbols.rust: Rust shared-reference borrows and Arc<TaskQueue> lifetime; queue.rs:166-181, 373-377
symbols.ownership_and_limits: Rust lifetime tracking replaces the C active-call atomic counter.
Owned standard-library containers release automatically on all construction rollback paths.
State transition and atomic cancellation update occur while holding the queue mutex.

Fixed worker count, bounded FIFO pending indices, cancellation/generation checks, completion publication under mutex, and context drop after unlock. A task transitioned to Running is invoked even if cancellation arrives before callback entry; cancellation suppresses publication. Canceled queued/stale work is discarded without invocation. Callback panics become failed results with value 0 so the worker remains alive.
symbols.adaptation: The test-only entry gate pauses after the Running transition and mutex release to exercise the C callback-entry cancellation race deterministically. Rust panic containment has no C equivalent.

symbols.ownership_and_limits: Preserves exact priority: invalid input, duplicate ID, stale generation, stopped queue, then full capacity. Queue state and pending indices are committed atomically under one mutex.
